key_concepts: Mixtures can be homogeneous (uniform) or heterogeneous (non-uniform).
A mixture of different seeds is heterogeneous and its components remain recognizable.
Salt dissolved in water forms a homogeneous mixture.
In a solution, a solute dissolves in a solvent.
Alcohol mixes well with water and forms a solution.
Cooking oil does not mix with water.
Food coloring added to water forms a homogeneous colored mixture.
Oil and colored water form a non-uniform mixture that separates after shaking.
Some liquid mixtures are uniform while others are non-uniform.
Suspensions are non-uniform mixtures that can separate upon standing.
